newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds await more dollar paper, Brazil global.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds await more dollar paper, Brazil global.

text.p: Primary market activity was slow on Friday, with news of upcoming emerging market bonds providing most of the focus.
Brazil completed a roadshow for its $750 million global bond, which traders said would be launched on Monday with a five-year maturity.
Spread talk was 255 to 275 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, with the final pricing expected at around 265 b.p. over.
The best comparable outstanding bond is a five-year issue launched by Brazil's state oil company Petrobras. This was trading at around 255 b.p. over on the bid, dealers said.
"A yield pick-up of 10 b.p. over Petrobras would make the paper look cheap," an emerging market investor said.
Russia is the next big event on the new issues calender, and today it said roadshows for a debut dollar bond would start on November 11.
After Russia got its ratings earlier this month, roadshows for the deal were expected to kick off a few weeks later.
But visa problems led to a delay, dealers said.
"Ideally they would have done the roadshows by the end of October, to allow plenty of time to launch the deal before the end of the year," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"But some Ministry of Finance officials had trouble getting visas on time, and this resulted in a delay," he said.
Demand for the Russia paper is expected to be strong, dealers said, with other borrowers from the country were lining up to tap the markets once the benchmark has been set.
These included Moscow and St Petersburg.
Spread talk remains in the mid-300s b.p. over, they said.
Other dollar bonds expected next week include a $250 million five-year bond for Hitachi and a $250 million 10-year deal for Japan Highway.
